publication.title: Computer Agent Arena: Toward Human-Centric Evaluation and Analysis of Computer-Use Agents

name: Computer Agent Arena: Toward Human-Centric Evaluation and Analysis of Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and abstract, the full proceedings PDF and the platform README at commit 4536036; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Two anonymized agents run the same user-written instruction in parallel, identically initialized Ubuntu or Windows virtual machines on AWS EC2, shown to users through a browser VNC view and synchronized replays; the paper turns the pairwise votes into a Bradley-Terry ranking and also collects optional step-level labels. It reports 2,201 filtered votes from 1,058 users over 12 agents, compares pure GUI agents with agents that also call tools or write code, and links github.com/xlang-ai/computer-agent-arena for the platform and a Hugging Face page for the collected data; neither release was reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Crowdsourced arena where users set tasks on cloud Ubuntu or Windows desktops, watch two anonymous computer-use agents attempt them side by side and vote; reports 2,201 votes over 12 agents.
